author: chatgpt-codex-connector
body:
Reject extend when lease is no longer latest generation
Manager.Extend only re-reads and rewrites the caller’s generation key, so a renewal can succeed even after another holder has already created a newer generation during the read/save window around expiry. In that case the old holder refreshes generation N while the new holder owns generation N+1, so both can believe they hold the lease (split-brain). This can occur when extend starts just before TTL expiry and a competing Acquire runs just after expiry but before m.save here; Extend should also verify that this lease is still the latest generation (or use a conditional write) before persisting the new expiry.
Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

author: renatolabs
body:
In the Release case, the read/validate/write happens due to a lack of a conditional write operation in the KV store. The consequence there is also pretty benign: a caller might not get ErrLeaseLost on concurrent Release() but whether it gets that error or not, it can correctly assume it no longer holds the lease.
In this case, we are potentially allowing two clients to believe the hold the same lease at the same time, the main property this library is supposed to provide. We shouldn't rely on callers calling Extend "well before expiry".
In the design doc for this package, Extend becomes a Create() with the next generation -- that is much safer as it guarantees a single lease holder.

author: renatolabs
body:
The Lost() channel on the lease has one main job: notifying when the caller lost the lease. It should only fire when it's guaranteed that the lease is lost. Now that I'm taking a closer look at Extend, I'm thinking that we shouldn't use time.AfterFunc() for this, it makes Extend() inherently racy. In the current code, we could have already notified the caller that they lost the lease even though we just extended it.
I'm wondering if we should, instead, handle extensions internally: when acquiring a lease, the caller can optionally specify if they want automated renewals. If they do, we start a background goroutine that will periodically extend the lease (using the same mechanism as Extend in the design doc) and notifyLoss() if we can't. If the caller doesn't want renewals, we can use a timer as we are currently doing.
Another advantage of this approach is that it unifies how renewals are implemented instead of leaving it up to callers, which would lead to multiple variations of the same logic.
I'm curious to hear @pstibrany's thoughts as I believe what I described above is closer to what search is doing at the moment.

author: renatolabs
body:
One issue I see with this loop is that it has no visibility of when the lease naturally expires. We're renewing (by default) every ttl / 3 and giving up to 3/4 of that for a renewal to succeed. Using 10s (default TTL) as an example gives us renewInterval = 3.3s and extendTimeout = 2.5s for a total of 5.8s per attempt.
By the time the second try kicks in, we could have a situation where someone else got the lease but this caller has not been notified that they lost the lease (there would be a gap that grows with the TTL).
TLDR: I think that if now() + extendTimeout > expiry, we should give up retrying and signal loss.
